title: Kamran Hekmati, Dual-National Jewish Citizen, Released from Evin Prison
content:
According to HRANA, citing Radio Farda, Kamran Hekmati was released from Evin Prison on the evening of Saturday, September 5, 2026.

According to the report, despite his release from prison, Mr. Hekmati remains subject to a ban on leaving the country and is currently in Iran.

No information has yet been released regarding the conditions of his release. However, it is believed that he may have been released after completing his prison sentence.

Mr. Hekmati has cancer. It was previously reported that he had been granted medical leave to pursue treatment. However, after approximately one month and before the end of his 45-day medical leave, he was returned to prison. His return took place before he could begin chemotherapy, raising concerns about his access to specialized medical care.
snippet: According to HRANA, citing Radio Farda, Kamran Hekmati was released from Evin Prison on the evening of Saturday, September 5, 2026.
sourceDescription: Human Rights Activists News Agency Hrana – News Agency | Human Rights Activists News Agency

title: Sanandaj: Fereydoun Namdari and Sholeh Rouhi Arrested by Security Forces
content:
According to HRANA, citing Kolbar News, two citizens have been arrested in Sanandaj.

The couple have been identified as Fereydoun Namdari, 55, and Sholeh Rouhi.

According to the report, on Sunday, September 6, approximately 15 Ministry of Intelligence agents went to Mr. Namdari’s workplace and arrested him by force and with violence, without presenting a judicial warrant. The agents subsequently went to his residence, conducted a thorough search of the premises, and arrested his wife, Sholeh Rouhi. She was also transferred to an undisclosed location.

At the time of this report, no information has been obtained regarding the reasons for their arrests, the charges brought against them, or their place of detention. The families’ efforts to obtain information about the couple’s condition and whereabouts have so far been unsuccessful.
snippet:
According to HRANA, citing Kolbar News, two citizens have been arrested in Sanandaj.

The couple have been identified as Fereydoun Namdari, 55, and Sholeh Rouhi.
sourceDescription: Human Rights Activists News Agency Hrana – News Agency | Human Rights Activists News Agency

title: At Least 10 Sunni Citizens Arrested in Ahvaz
content:
According to HRANA, ton Friday, September 4, 2026, intelligence forces entered a private residence in the Kuy-e Mashali neighborhood of Ahvaz and arrested at least 10 Sunni Arab citizens.

According to information received by HRANA, the citizens had gathered at the home of a friend for a meeting when intelligence forces surrounded the residence and entered the premises. During the raid, the forces beat several of those present and arrested them. The detainees were subsequently transferred to an undisclosed location.

HRANA has so far confirmed the identities of three of the detainees: Razi Heydari, 50; Hossein Heydari, 29; and Abdolhadi Asakereh, 30. The identities of the other detainees are still being investigated.

These citizens are residents of the Kuy-e Mashali and Akhar Asfalt neighborhoods of Ahvaz.

At the time of this report, despite several days having passed since their arrest, no information has been obtained regarding the detainees’ whereabouts or the charges brought against them.
snippet: According to HRANA, ton Friday, September 4, 2026, intelligence forces entered a private residence in the Kuy-e Mashali neighborhood of Ahvaz and arrested at least 10 Sunni Arab citizens.
sourceDescription: Human Rights Activists News Agency Hrana – News Agency | Human Rights Activists News Agency

title: Shaker Bouri Sentenced to Prison and Fine
content:
According to HRANA, Shaker Bouri has been sentenced to imprisonment and a fine.

According to a verdict issued by Branch 101 of the Criminal Court II of Abadan and formally communicated to him, Bouri was sentenced to 13 months and 20 days in prison on the charge of “disseminating false information with the intent to cause harm to others.” On a separate charge of “insulting a member of the Islamic Consultative Assembly,” he was ordered to pay a fine of 45 million rials.

Under Article 134 of the Islamic Penal Code, the most severe punishment, in this case, the prison sentence, will be enforceable.

The case was opened in connection with the publication of video content following a complaint filed against Shaker Bouri by Mousa Ghazanfarabadi, a member of the Islamic Consultative Assembly.

Shaker Bouri, a satirist residing in Abadan, has previously been arrested in connection with his activities.
snippet: According to HRANA, Shaker Bouri has been sentenced to imprisonment and a fine.
sourceDescription: Human Rights Activists News Agency Hrana – News Agency | Human Rights Activists News Agency

title: January 2026 Protests: Abolfazl Rostami and Erfan Moradi Dangi Each Sentenced to Five Years in Prison
content:
According to HRANA, citing Kolbar News, Abolfazl Rostami and Erfan Moradi Dangi have been sentenced to prison.

According to the report, Branch 1 of the Revolutionary Court of Qasr-e Shirin recently sentenced each of these citizens to five years in prison on the charge of “assembly and collusion to commit a crime against national security.” The sentences have been formally communicated to them.

The two citizens were arrested in Qasr-e Shirin, Kermanshah Province, on Thursday, May 28, 2026, by forces of the IRGC Intelligence Organization in connection with the January 2026 protests. After several weeks in detention and under interrogation, they were released temporarily on bail pending the completion of judicial proceedings.

The report states that Abolfazl Rostami and Erfan Moradi Dangi were subjected to pressure as well as physical and psychological torture during their detention.
snippet: According to HRANA, citing Kolbar News, Abolfazl Rostami and Erfan Moradi Dangi have been sentenced to prison.
sourceDescription: Human Rights Activists News Agency Hrana – News Agency | Human Rights Activists News Agency

title: Siamak Mofidi and Soroush Enayati, Two Teenagers, Arrested in Takab
content:
According to HRANA, citing Kurdpa, two teenagers have been arrested in Takab County. They have been identified as Siamak Mofidi, 17, and Soroush Enayati, 16, both residents of Takab.

According to the report, on the evening of Saturday, September 5, 2026, security forces entered the teenagers’ homes without presenting a judicial warrant, arrested them, and transferred them to an undisclosed location. They were subsequently transferred to an unspecified location in Tehran for interrogation.

The report states that the two teenagers had been working at a café in Tehran in recent months.

As of the time of this report, no information has been obtained regarding the reasons for their arrest, the agency responsible for their detention, the charges against them, or their exact place of detention. They have also been denied access to legal counsel and have not been permitted to contact or meet with their families.
snippet: According to HRANA, citing Kurdpa, two teenagers have been arrested in Takab County. They have been identified as Siamak Mofidi, 17, and Soroush Enayati, 16, both residents of Takab.
sourceDescription: Human Rights Activists News Agency Hrana – News Agency | Human Rights Activists News Agency

title: Three Citizens Arrested in Shadegan Over Social Media Posts
content:
According to HRANA, citing IRNA, three citizens were arrested by police forces in Shadgan, Khuzestan province.

According to the report, following the publication of content on social media allegedly intended to “disturb public opinion, undermine public morale, and spread propaganda against the Islamic Republic,” Shadgan County’s Public Security and Intelligence Police initiated efforts to identify and arrest the individuals.

Rouhollah Ashiri, the police commander of Shadgan, stated that after being identified and with judicial authorization, the individuals were arrested by the Public Security and Intelligence Police and Shadgan Police Station No. 11.

He claimed that following their arrest and during interrogation, the individuals confessed to the alleged offenses and were subsequently referred to the judicial authorities for further legal proceedings.

The report did not disclose the identities of the detainees, their place of detention, or their current status.
snippet: According to HRANA, citing IRNA, three citizens were arrested by police forces in Shadgan, Khuzestan province.
sourceDescription: Human Rights Activists News Agency Hrana – News Agency | Human Rights Activists News Agency

title: Ali Babaei, Azerbaijani-Turk Activist, Sentenced to 9 Months in Prison
content:
According to HRANA, Ali Babaei, an Azerbaijani-Turk activist currently held in Tabriz Prison, has been sentenced to prison.

Mr. Babaei was sentenced by Branch 1 of the Tabriz Revolutionary Court to nine months in prison on the charge of “propaganda against the regime.” According to information received by HRANA, this sentence relates to a case opened against him following his arrest in January 2026.

An informed source familiar with the case confirmed the news to HRANA, stating that Mr. Babaei’s arrest in January was intended to prevent him from engaging in activities related to the protests taking place at the time.

The hearing on the charges against this Azerbaijani-Turk activist was held yesterday before the aforementioned branch.

In June 2025, in a separate case, Mr. Babaei was tried alongside 12 other citizens by Branch 2 of the Tabriz Revolutionary Court. In late December 2025, he was subsequently sentenced to two years and nine months in prison on the charge of “membership in an illegal group” and three years and seven months on the charge of “assembly and collusion against national security.”

In May 2026, the East Azerbaijan Province Court of Appeals upheld the ruling in full.
snippet: According to HRANA, Ali Babaei, an Azerbaijani-Turk activist currently held in Tabriz Prison, has been sentenced to prison.
sourceDescription: Human Rights Activists News Agency Hrana – News Agency | Human Rights Activists News Agency

title: Writer Roozbeh Gilasian Sentenced to Prison
content:
According to HRANA, Roozbeh Gilasian has been sentenced to prison.

Under a ruling issued on Wednesday, September 2, 2026, by Branch 1 of the Bandar Abbas Revolutionary Court, Mr. Gilasian was sentenced to eight months in prison on the charge of “propaganda against the regime” and four years in prison on the charge of “engaging in educational activities and/or deviant propaganda and/or activities disruptive to the sacred principles of Islam.”

According to information received by HRANA, managing a channel with approximately 100 members and sharing several books that he had previously written and published were among the acts cited as grounds for the charges against Mr. Gilasian.

An informed source close to the writer’s family confirmed the news to HRANA and said: “A number of citizens in Bandar Abbas were arrested following the 12-day war. During the proceedings in their cases, Mr. Gilasian’s name and writings came to the attention of security agencies. He was subsequently arrested as well and faced charges related to the activities of this channel and his works.”

Mr. Gilasian was arrested by security forces in Gorgan in August 2025 and was subsequently released on bail.
snippet: According to HRANA, Roozbeh Gilasian has been sentenced to prison.
sourceDescription: Human Rights Activists News Agency Hrana – News Agency | Human Rights Activists News Agency

title: Artin Ghazanfari Remains in Legal Limbo and Denied Medical Treatment at Greater Tehran Prison
content:
According to HRANA,Artin Ghazanfari, a Baha’i citizen, remains in detention.

An informed source close to his family confirmed the news to HRANA, saying: “Artin Ghazanfari has been held in legal limbo at Greater Tehran Prison for more than seven months. Mr. Ghazanfari suffers from several medical conditions, including heart failure, asthma, and high blood pressure. Despite the health problems caused by these conditions, he has yet to receive effective medical care.”

The source added: “His family’s efforts to secure his temporary release on bail for medical leave have also been unsuccessful. He requires appropriate medical care and transfer to a medical facility outside the prison.”

On July 29, 2026, a court session addressing the charges against this Baha’i citizen was held before Branch 14 of the Tehran Revolutionary Court.

Mr. Ghazanfari was arrested on January 19, 2026, at his home in Tehran. At the same time, agents searched his home and workplace and confiscated a number of electronic devices, books, work equipment, and personal belongings.

Artin Ghazanfari, a Baha’i citizen and photojournalist, has previously served a prison sentence in connection with his activities.
snippet: According to HRANA,Artin Ghazanfari, a Baha’i citizen, remains in detention.
sourceDescription: Human Rights Activists News Agency Hrana – News Agency | Human Rights Activists News Agency

title: Four Prisoners Executed in Vakilabad Prison in Mashhad and Gorgan Prison
content:
According to HRANA, citing Iran Human Rights Organization, four prisoners were executed in Vakilabad Prison in Mashhad and Gorgan Prison at dawn on Wednesday, September 2, 2026.

The prisoners have been identified as Ahmad Haji-Hassani, 50, married, a father of four, and a resident of Gonbad-e Kavus; Omid Rakhshani, 22, from Mashhad; and Ansar Nami, 52, and Nazif Rasoul Khandeh, 46, both from Taloqan, Afghanistan.

According to the report, Ahmad Haji-Hassani was hanged in Gorgan Prison. He had previously been arrested on drug-related charges for “transporting eight kilograms and 700 grams of methamphetamine” and was subsequently sentenced to death by a Revolutionary Court.

Omid Rakhshani, Ansar Nami, and Nazif Rasoul Khandeh were executed in Vakilabad Prison in Mashhad. Rakhshani had been arrested approximately three years earlier on a murder charge and was subsequently sentenced to death by the judiciary.

Ansar Nami and Nazif Rasoul Khandeh, both Afghan nationals, were arrested two years ago on a murder charge in a joint case and were later sentenced to death by the judiciary.

The two Afghan nationals were executed without being granted a final visit with their families.
snippet: According to HRANA, citing Iran Human Rights Organization, four prisoners were executed in Vakilabad Prison in Mashhad and Gorgan Prison at dawn on Wednesday, September 2, 2026.
sourceDescription: Human Rights Activists News Agency Hrana – News Agency | Human Rights Activists News Agency

title: Three Baha’i Citizens Remain Detained in Legal Limbo at Tir Kola Prison in Sari
content:
According to HRANA, the news agency of Human Rights Activists in Iran, Soraya Manouchehrzadeh, Shima Sanaei, and Fakhereh Zahedi remain in prison.

Two weeks have passed since the arrest of these three Baha’i citizens, and they continue to be held in legal limbo at Tir Kola Prison in Sari. According to information received by HRANA, they have been permitted to make only one phone call to their families during this period.

An informed source familiar with their situation told HRANA: “According to their families, interrogations of the three citizens at the Ministry of Intelligence’s detention facility in Sari produced no substantial evidence against them. Nevertheless, in recent days, several of their neighbors have been summoned to the Ministry’s intelligence office.”

The families of the three citizens also learned, three days after their arrests, that Amin Nasrollah-Chamani, an investigator with Branch 7 of the Sari Revolutionary Prosecutor’s Office, had set bail at two billion tomans for each of them. However, despite the bail being secured and guarantors being introduced, the judicial authority’s administrative office refused to register it.
snippet: According to HRANA, the news agency of Human Rights Activists in Iran, Soraya Manouchehrzadeh, Shima Sanaei, and Fakhereh Zahedi remain in prison.
sourceDescription: Human Rights Activists News Agency Hrana – News Agency | Human Rights Activists News Agency

title: Prisoner Executed in Lakan Prison, Rasht
content:
According to HRANA, citing Iran Human Rights Organization, a prisoner was executed in Lakan Prison in Rasht at dawn on Monday, August 31, 2026.

The prisoner has been identified as Mojtaba Salahi Laghani, a resident of Laghan village in Shaft County.

According to the report, Mr. Salahi was arrested approximately four years ago on a murder charge and was subsequently sentenced to death by the judiciary.

According to HRA’s Annual Report, in 2025 at least 2,063 citizens, including 61 women and 2 juvenile offenders, were executed. Of these, the sentences of 11 individuals were carried out in public. During the same period, 172 other individuals were sentenced to death.
snippet: According to HRANA, citing Iran Human Rights Organization, a prisoner was executed in Lakan Prison in Rasht at dawn on Monday, August 31, 2026.
sourceDescription: Human Rights Activists News Agency Hrana – News Agency | Human Rights Activists News Agency

title: January 2026 Protests: Saman Ghaderi Sentenced to 14 Years in Prison
content:
According to HRANA, Saman Ghaderi has been sentenced to imprisonment.

According to a ruling issued by Branch 26 of the Tehran Revolutionary Court, presided over by Judge Iman Afshari, and served on Mr. Ghaderi on Tuesday, August 25, he was sentenced to 11 years in prison on the charge of “acting against national security” and three years on the charge of “insulting the sacred.”

An informed source close to the family of the political defendant confirmed the news to HRANA and said: “Following the notification of the ruling, Mr. Ghaderi challenged the verdict and filed an appeal.”

Saman Ghaderi was arrested in Tehran in March 2026 by agents of the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps Intelligence Organization in connection with the January 2026 protests. After completing the initial stages of interrogation, he was transferred to the Greater Tehran Prison.

Saman Ghaderi is 37 years old and from Urmia.
snippet: According to HRANA, Saman Ghaderi has been sentenced to imprisonment.
sourceDescription: Human Rights Activists News Agency Hrana – News Agency | Human Rights Activists News Agency

title: Record of HRA’s Germany Accountability Initiative
content: HRANA– In September 2026, Human Rights Activists in Iran (HRA) launched a legal and advocacy initiative aimed at advancing accountability for alleged crimes against humanity committed by Iranian State authorities. At the center of this effort was HRA’s submission to Germany’s Federal Prosecutor General requesting the opening of a structural investigation (Strukturermittlungsverfahren) into the situation in Iran, with a particular evidentiary focus on the repression surrounding the nationwide protests of December 2025 and January 2026.
snippet: HRANA– In September 2026, Human Rights Activists in Iran (HRA) launched a legal and advocacy initiative aimed at advancing accountability for alleged crimes against humanity committed by Iranian State
